author: Stephanie Kirchgaessner
description:
Jamie Raskin says ‘startling’ email asked whether young woman was ‘for me, or are you keeping her for yourself’

A powerful Democratic lawmaker has called for a criminal investigation into former Bard College president Leon Botstein after congressional investigators uncovered an email from Botstein to accused sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein in which he says Botstein asked if a young woman was “for me, or are you keeping her for yourself”.

The latest development appears to have triggered the immediate resignation of Botstein from all Bard-affiliated positions, including his professorship and roles in Bard’s music programs. Botstein had led the college for 50 years and only recently stepped down as president.

Continue reading...
title: Leon Botstein resigns from Bard roles as key Democrat demands investigation into Epstein links

author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
description:
Hundred-and-fifty-year-old Wych elm in Newcastle, Co Down has grown sideways owing to strong winds

The “astonishing and bizarre” Bendy Tree in Northern Ireland has been crowned the winner of this year’s tree of the year competition.

The wych elm tree, located in Newcastle, County Down, owes its name to its near horizontal trunk, which has grown sideways owing to the strong seaside winds coming off the Irish Sea.

Continue reading...
title: Bendy elm still standing against all odds crowned UK tree of the year

author: Robert Mackey
description:
Ads promoting the president have cost more than $12m and his Super Pac has refused to reimburse taxpayers

  • Sign up to The Stakes 2026: your weekly guide to the US midterms

The Democratic National Committee sued the Trump administration in federal court on Wednesday, asking a judge in Washington to stop the president from using taxpayer funds to air a series of ads promoting himself, arguing that the ads are illegal government-sponsored propaganda.

The ads promoting Donald Trump, including one recycled from his 2024 presidential campaign, have cost taxpayers more than $12m so far, according to the media tracking firm AdImpact.
title: Democrats sue to stop Trump from using taxpayer funds for self-promoting ads

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Jamaal Howard’s lawyers urge halt, citing risk of another failed execution after Pike’s ordeal in Tennessee

Texas on Wednesday is scheduled to carry out the first execution in the US after the the botched lethal injection of Christa Pike in Tennessee last week.

Lawyers for Jamaal Howard, a Texas man on death row for capital murder, are seeking to halt the execution, arguing there are similar risks as in the case of Pike.

Continue reading...
title: Texas set to carry out first US execution since botched lethal injection of Christa Pike

author: Ariana Baio
description:
President floats firing Chris LaCivita and James Blair over any ‘conflict’ after reports of work in Republika Srpska

Donald Trump distanced himself from two top advisers on Wednesday, claiming he did not have “any idea who else they work for”, after it was reported they spent the weekend assisting a pro-Russia government in the Balkans.

On Truth Social, Trump wrote that Chris LaCivita, the co-manager of his 2024 presidential campaign, and James Blair, a campaign adviser and White House deputy chief of staff on leave of absence, “are outside consultants” and “do not work for me other than as outside consultants”.
title: Trump backs away from top aides who reportedly advised pro-Russia government

author: Sam Levin in Los Angeles
description:
Bernadette Greene-Placentia says she is sharing her story in order to fight for victims of sexual assault

This article contains graphic descriptions of sexual assault.

A congressional candidate in Arizona says she was attacked and raped in August while trying to repair one of her damaged campaign signs.

Information and support for anyone affected by rape or sexual abuse issues is available from the following organizations. In the US, Rainn offers support on 800-656-4673. In the UK, Rape Crisis offers support on 0808 500 2222. In Australia, support is available at 1800Respect (1800 737 732). Other international helplines can be found at ibiblio.org/rcip/internl.html
title: Arizona congressional candidate says she was raped while trying to repair campaign sign

author: Heather Stewart Economics editor
description:
The Tory leader’s proposal to slash the tax would shovel £6bn of taxpayer money to the already-wealthy

Kemi Badenoch’s inheritance tax gambit is a Conservative classic. After all, it was George Osborne’s high-profile pledge to “take the family home out of inheritance tax” in 2007 that put Gordon Brown off calling a snap general election.

In practice, Osborne’s plan involved a £1m threshold for inheritance tax – and given the global financial crisis had blown a hole in the public finances by the time the Conservative-Lib Dem coalition came to power in 2010, it never came to pass.

Continue reading...
title: Badenoch’s inheritance tax gambit makes no economic sense | Heather Stewart

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Texas attorney general acknowledged affordability was his party’s ‘biggest problem’ heading into the midterms

  • US politics live – latest updates

Ken Paxton, the Texas attorney general running as the Republican candidate in a competitive Senate race, admitted privately that rising fuel prices as a result of Donald Trump’s Iran war were hurting his party before the midterms in the latest leaked audio recording.

Asked what issues were “dragging” his campaign at a closed-door fundraising event, Paxton replied, “It’s not tariffs … it’s the war, it’s gas prices, it’s diesel,” according to an audio recording
title: Paxton admits Trump’s Iran war and US gas prices are plaguing Republicans in leaked audio

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
Four people and a dog may have been exposed to rabies from the animal, Los Angeles public health officials say

Los Angeles county recently documented its first rabid raccoon in more than 50 years, and health officials are urging residents to never touch wild animals.

The county’s department of public health announced in a statement this week that four people and a dog may have been exposed to the animal at a back yard work site in the city of Westlake Village. The raccoon appeared in ill-health but was not aggressive.

Continue reading...
title: LA officials document first case of a rabid raccoon in more than 50 years

author: Melissa Davey Medical editor
description:
The number of pharmacies stocking the MS-2 Step medication increased from 2,228 to 4,107 after rules relaxed in 2023

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The number of Australian pharmacies stocking an abortion pill increased by almost 50% when prescribing restrictions were relaxed, with researchers saying the findings suggest deregulation of abortion promotes safer and faster healthcare.

A study published in the medical journal JAMA Network Open on Thursday examined the impact of changes by the Therapeutic Goods Administration in 2023 which meant the medication, MS-2 Step, could be prescribed by any GP.
title: Abortion pill access jumps almost 50% after Australia eases restrictions for pharmacies

author: Petra Stock
description:
Researchers found the shift from open woodland to dense forest after 1788 led to more intense fires, consistent with loss of cultural burning practices

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

The drastic land use changes wreaked by colonisation created a “catastrophic wildfire loop” that rendered south-east Australia more susceptible to climate-fuelled bushfires, experts say.

A team of researchers, working with the Gunaikurnai Land and Waters Aboriginal Corporation, an organisation that represents traditional owners, reconstructed 1,000 years of vegetation and fire history at Purghagoolah, a lake surrounded by forest in Croajingolong national park in Gippsland, Victoria.
title: ‘Catastrophic wildfire loop’ after colonisation left parts of Australia more at risk from bushfires, study finds

author: Peter Walker, Pippa Crerar, Rowena Mason and Jessica Elgot
description:
At Conservative conference, some worry about becoming a one-woman party, while others say party should thank their lucky stars they have her

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Kemi Badenoch has long said that the Conservatives were “under new management”, but in a TV interview to mark the end of a party conference at which she has been front and centre of more or less everything, she took the analogy further.

“Your viewers will know that sometimes you have a football team that’s disappointing,” the Tory leader told GB News. “There’s a new captain, there’s a new coach, there’s a new owner, effectively – which is all me.”

Continue reading...
title: ‘All me’: Tory party riding high on Kemi Badenoch’s wave of popularity

author: Dan Sabbagh
description:
Veteran leftwinger has been ‘in exile in the east’ in Russia and not been to Holborn and St Pancras constituency since campaign began

George Galloway has been elected seven times to parliament, but his attempt to succeed for an eighth this week, in the London seat formerly held by Keir Starmer, is undoubtedly his most curious effort yet.

Since the byelection campaign began, the leader of the Workers party of Britain has yet to set foot in the UK, let alone the Holborn and St Pancras constituency, because he is in what he describes as “self-exile” after being questioned by counter-terrorism police at Gatwick airport a year ago.

Continue reading...
title: George Galloway contests London byelection without setting foot in UK

author: Adam Gabbatt
description:
NAACP files lawsuit after head of DoJ’s civil rights division says she hopes to send election monitors to polls

The Trump administration has been sued over its plans to deploy “a historic number” of election monitors to polling stations during next month’s midterm elections.

The bid “stands to jeopardize” the elections and could “interfere with the right of voters to participate in the election free from intimidation”, according to the NAACP, which filed a lawsuit against Harmeet Dhillon, head of the justice department’s civil rights division, who has said she hopes to send 1,000 monitors to midterm polling sites in November.

Continue reading...
title: Trump administration sued over plans to send election monitors to voting sites

author: Oliver Holmes in Bangkok
description:
New ‘support and training centre’ prompts concern in region but China says it is ‘not directed at any third party’

Satellite images show attack jets stationed at a new overseas Chinese military facility in Laos, which opened last week and gives Beijing’s air force its first foothold in mainland south-east Asia.

Images provided by the commercial satellite provider Vantor show eight light attack aircraft positioned at Ban Keun airport alongside what appear to be more than a dozen military vehicles lined up in rows.

Continue reading...
title: Satellite images show attack jets at Chinese military facility in Laos

author: Katherine Butler associate editor, Europe
description:
The big question facing ​A​ndy Burnham is not whether Brexit has harmed Britain, but if a rapidly changing Europe will keep the door open​ if the UK decides it wants back in

• Don’t get This Is Europe delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

It was lobbed into the national conversation without fanfare or warning, almost a footnote in the UK prime minister’s first speech as leader to his governing Labour party’s annual conference. But Andy Burnham has kicked off a quiet U-turn on Brexit.

By stating bluntly that the decision to leave Europe’s core political community had done “more harm than good”, Burnham broke a taboo in his own party, in effect, discarding his predecessor’s paralysing ‘red lin
title: Could the UK really rejoin the EU?

author: Adam Morton in Nadi, Fiji
description:
It isn’t hard to see a contradiction between the PM’s message in Fiji and his opposition to legal action to stop a NSW coalmine

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

There are unlikely to be many bigger moments in Australian action on the climate crisis this year than a judgment by the high court on Wednesday.

In what is likely to prove a historic victory, the court sided with community members in the Hunter Valley to strike down a state regulator’s approval of a massive coalmine expansion that could have kept it operating until 2048.
title: Overseas, Albanese sees ‘the very definition of climate injustice’ – but at home, he still wants coal

author: Chris Osuh
description:
Gathering expected to take place at Richmond Terrace, opposite Downing Street, at 5pm on Wednesday

British Jewish organisations will gather in central London for a vigil honouring victims of the 7 October attacks in Israel on Wednesday, after a day of tributes from politicians and community leaders.

A 5pm vigil is expected to take place at Richmond Terrace, opposite Downing Street.

Continue reading...
title: British Jewish groups to hold London vigil for victims of 7 October attacks

author: Pippa Crerar Political editor
description:
Party hopes to win over affluent middle-class voters as Badenoch rejects calls to ‘unite the right’ in conference speech

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Kemi Badenoch has announced the Conservatives would abolish inheritance tax on family homes if elected, prompting immediate criticism that she is prioritising cutting taxes for the rich.

The Tory leader also said couples would be able to leave behind an additional £1m tax-free to their families, as the party attempts to shore up its traditional base in southern England.

Continue reading...
title: Tories accused of prioritising rich voters as Badenoch lays out inheritance tax cut plan

author: Guardian staff and agency
description:
Immigration enforcement agency has signed $16.7m deal for devices that induced ‘excessive’ fear in military subjects

The electric-shock gloves immigration agents could soon use to control detainees and protesters worked so powerfully during a military exercise that participants felt intense pain, stopped fighting immediately and feared additional exposures, according to a previously unreleased army study.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) leaders were aware of the findings before signing a $16.7m contract in August to purchase 6,000 pairs of shock gloves, according to records obtained by the watchdog group American Oversight and shared with the Associated Press.

Continue reading...
title: Electric-shock gloves ICE plans to use inflicted intense pain in army study

author: José Olivares
description:
At least 73 people estimated to have joined protest against prolonged detention and Folkston facility’s ‘violations’

A group of people detained inside a privately-run Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) jail in Georgia have launched a mass hunger strike this week to protest against their prolonged detention and the facility’s conditions, according to advocates and family members.

Advocates estimate at least 73 detained immigrants are participating in the hunger strike inside the Folkston D Ray James ICE processing center in south-east Georgia. The Folkston facility, a former state prison, is run by the private prison company GEO Group under a contract with ICE.

Continue reading...
title: Detained immigrants at Georgia ICE facility launch mass hunger strike

author: Martin Belam
description:
Site of the Nova music festival near Re’im one of the locations where grieving relatives have gathered. Plus, the unlikely legal tussle over a ‘brain rot’ meme

Good morning. Israel is holding ceremonies and gatherings to mark the third anniversary of the 7 October attack by Hamas, in which about 1,200 people were killed and another 251 taken captive to Gaza. Israeli communities shattered by the massacres, torn between rebuilding their lives and remembering lost friends and relatives, have spoken to Emma Graham-Harrison about their experiences of that day and the days since. The Guardian is marking the day with a live blog, featuring the latest images of events taking place in Israel and around the world.

I
title: Israel marks third anniversary of 7 October Hamas attacks | First Thing

author: Jordyn Beazley
description:
Anne Twomey says $6m for Marrickville golf club given under ‘farcical scheme’, which Labor has defended as within rules

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

A leading constitutional expert has labelled an Albanese government decision to award a $6m grant to a golf club in the prime minister’s electorate as “grey corruption” and called the scheme under which it was given a “farce”.

Anne Twomey, a University of Sydney professor emerita, submitted the scathing assessment to a Senate inquiry into an opaque $560m invitation-only grants scheme used to fund projects Labor promised at the 2025 election, and which largely went to Labor-held seats.
title: Constitutional expert labels Albanese government’s golf club grant ‘grey corruption’

author: Jon Henley in Paris
description:
Minister says use of grenades has been stopped ‘until we know what happened’ as protests across France continue

  • How dilapidated are French schools and how bad is inequality in the education system?

  • Europe live – latest updates

France is suspending the use of stun grenades by police at high-school demonstrations, the interior minister has said, amid mounting accusations of police brutality during a fortnight of protests marred by often violent clashes that have injured hundreds.

Laurent Nuñez told RTL radio on Wednesday that he had ordered a temporary halt to t
title: French police suspend use of stun grenades after high-school protester loses hand

author: Amelia Gentleman
description:
Lawyers launch super-complaint after gathering evidence suggesting officers frequently dismiss image-based abuse

Police forces are routinely failing to investigate complaints about the circulation of image-based abuse, previously known as “revenge pornography”, according to research that has triggered a super-complaint over the way such crimes are handled.

Lawyers have gathered evidence from 100 people who reported intimate images being shared online without their consent. Their research suggests that image-based abuse is still frequently dismissed or not recognised as criminal offending, despite being described by the former prime minister Keir Starmer as a national emergency.

Continue reading...
title: Police routinely failing to investigate ‘revenge porn’ reports, research shows

author: Joanna Partridge
description:
Average cost of home in September was £298,441, says Lloyds – about the same as year earlier and in August

  • Business live – latest updates

UK house prices flatlined in September, according to a leading index, as rising mortgage costs started to weigh on the market.

The average cost of a home was £298,441, roughly the same as it was a year earlier and in the previous month, according to the tracker from Lloyds previously known as the Halifax HPI.

Continue reading...
title: UK house prices flatline as rising mortgage costs weigh on market

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
Ukraine president confirms series of attacks on Pryluky, Dnipro, Kremenchik, Zaporizhzhia and Kyiv

Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia launched “one fo the most vile strikes” on Ukraine last night, targeting the country’s energy infrastructure overnight.

At least 11 people were killed, and more than 34 injured in a series of attacks on Pryluky, Dnipro, Kremenchik, Zaporizhzhia, and Kyiv, which Zelenskyy ironically called “a birthday gift for Putin” who turns 74 today.

“On Putin’s birthday, Russian generals brought him his favorite present: war crimes.”

“What Russian generals fail to tell Putin is that he is not winning this war and never will. …

I urge all partners to give Putin real presents that will help him finally choose diplomacy over war. Stronger sanctions on his military-industrial complex, including facilities producing ballistic missile
title: At least 11 dead, 34 injured after ‘vile’ attack on Ukraine on Putin’s birthday, Zelenskyy says – Europe live

author: Jess Cartner-Morley in Paris
description:
Models walk runway at the Louvre with flying cars hovering above as designer envisions city life in a warming world

In silk slip dresses, breezy vented tunics and gossamer layers of chiffon, the models on Louis Vuitton’s catwalk were perfectly dressed for an unseasonably warm October evening in Paris. As the show began at sunset it was still 24C.

This summer’s record temperatures were on designer Nicolas Ghesquiière’s mind. “The world is getting warmer, this definitely had a strong influence” he said.

Continue reading...
title: Nicolas Ghesquière takes us into the future for Louis Vuitton show in Paris

author: Donna Lu, Lisa Cox, and Adam Morton
description:
High court finding in favour of Hunter Valley community group sets precedent other environmentalists should follow, advocate says

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

A landmark decision in Australia’s first climate change high court case has been described as a clear message to governments and fossil fuel companies that exported greenhouse gas emissions “cannot simply be ignored”.

On Wednesday morning, the nation’s highest court ruled that the approval of MACH Energy’s Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion in NSW’s Hunter Valley was invalid, in a judgment that sets a precedent for fossil fuel projects in the state.
title: ‘Lawyers should be running to courts’ to stop coal approvals after landmark ruling, NSW MP says

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Angus Taylor says opposition ‘worked closely’ with Parliamentary Budget Office but Liberal sources say it has not yet conducted a full analysis of the policy

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Coalition MPs concede the party’s newly released immigration policy has not been costed in full by the Parliamentary Budget Office (PBO), despite Angus Taylor defending the plan as “budget neutral”.

Taylor, and the deputy Liberal leader, Jane Hume, have said repeatedly the Coalition “worked closely” with the independent budget watchdog on its
title: Coalition MPs concede immigration pledge not fully costed by independent watchdog

author: Ben Smee
description:
Uneeb Ullah, 28, from Ipswich, has been remanded in custody after his arrest on Tuesday evening for the alleged murder of the child

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Queensland man has been charged with the murder of his three-month-old baby son, after the boy died in hospital this week.

The infant, from the Ipswich area west of Brisbane, died almost a week after being taken to hospital with “significant internal injuries”. The boy had been on life support.

This story was amended on 7 October 2026. A previous version incorrectly stated Uneeb Ullah was from Logan

Continue reading...<
title: Queensland man charged with murder after three-month-old son dies from ‘significant internal injuries’

author: Eva Corlett in Auckland and Adeshola Ore in Melbourne
description:
Hamam al-Hammami spent 175 days in New Zealand until May 2019, as Australian Jewish group calls for full investigation into his time in Melbourne

New Zealand authorities have launched their own investigation into the flydubai co-pilot who allegedly tried to hijack an Israel-bound plane, after police confirmed he underwent flight training there about a year after he abandoned a degree in Australia.

Disaster was narrowly averted on 30 September when passengers and crew intervened to stop the alleged attempt of the co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, 29, to take control of a flight to Tel Aviv with 182 people onboard.

Continue reading...
title: Flydubai attack investigation widens as alleged hijacker’s training in New Zealand scrutinised

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
NSW police officer has pleaded not guilty to murdering his ex and Luke Davies in a Sydney terrace in February 2024

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Despite an alleged obsession with his ex, Beau Lamarre-Condon never spoke about him to a close friend in the three months before allegedly murdering him, a jury has heard.

Lamarre-Condon, 31, has pleaded not guilty to murdering his ex-partner Jesse Baird and the man’s new boyfriend Luke Davies in a Sydney terrace in February 2024.

Continue reading...
title: Beau Lamarre-Condon didn’t talk about Jesse Baird to friend in lead-up to alleged murders, court hears

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Owens sued over September Instagram post that suggested trio tampered with evidence in death of Mississippi teen

Three friends of Nolan Wells, a Mississippi teen who died after a July boating trip, have sued NFL Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for defamation.

On 26 September, Owens shared an Instagram video that suggested Wells’s friends Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo and Morgan Seymour had deleted evidence from Wells’s phone after his death, which the three men denied in their lawsuit.

Continue reading...
title: Friends of Nolan Wells sue NFL Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for defamation

author: Robert Tait in Washington
description:
Republican challenged by Democrat Troy Jackson in critical Senate race says she opposes Iran war and Canada tariffs

Susan Collins, the Republican senator for Maine, pointedly distanced herself from Donald Trump in a televised debate with Democratic challenger Troy Jackson on Tuesday, as she sought to present an image of independence in a state that has voted against Trump three times.

Proclaiming herself as not the US president’s “favorite senator”, Collins made the highly unusual boast for a Republican that she had voted with Joe Biden, a Democrat, more than 90% of the time when he was president. She also emphasized her differences with her fellow Republicans, saying she voted against her own party more than any other senator.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Not exactly his favorite senator’: Susan Collins distances herself from Trump in Maine debate

author: Lisa Cox Environment and climate correspondent
description:
Ruling on Mount Pleasant coalmine shows ‘we cannot continue to dig up coal … and pretend the consequences have nothing to do with us’, group says

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Hunter Valley community group has won Australia’s first high court case to consider climate change, in a ruling advocates say sets a binding national precedent for fossil fuel projects in New South Wales.

In a landmark judgment, the nation’s highest court ruled that the approval of MACH Energy’s Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion in Musswellbrook was invalid.

Continue reading...
title: Hunter Valley community group wins landmark high court climate change case over Mount Pleasant coalmine

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Entertainer alleges complaint made about ‘in-kind’ donations over Victorian fundraisers, where he has been railing against Labor

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Dave Hughes says he will no longer be taking the stage at Victorian Liberal events, claiming the party decided having him on the bill could run afoul of the state’s political donation laws.

The comedian, better known as Hughesy, once described himself as a lifelong Labor voter, but has become a vocal critic of the party following May’s federal budget, which included
title: Comedian Dave Hughes to stop speaking at Liberal party events over political donation concerns

author: Jeremy Barr
description:
Ellison admits ‘good relationship’ with administration in remarks to reporters about newly merged media company

David Ellison, the chief executive of the newly formed media conglomerate Skydance, denied that he has “politicized” the company despite the close connection he has forged with Donald Trump’s White House over the 20 months of his administration.

“We have a good relationship with this administration,” Ellison acknowledged to reporters at a Tuesday press briefing focused on the now-consummated merger of Paramount Skydance and CNN parent company Warner Bros Discovery.

Continue reading...
title: David Ellison denies he has ‘politicized’ Skydance despite close Trump links

author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
description:
Australian adults again able to access the world’s most popular porn site after parent company introduces age checking via Apple devices

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian adults will be able to access Pornhub once again after the site brought in age-checking on Apple devices in response to legal requirements that initially saw the site block users.

In March, Aylo, the parent company of the most popular porn site on the internet,
title: Pornhub returns to Australia after banning access due to age verification rules

author: Alex Daniel
description:
Latest model is launching in New York to target rich US buyers – and is more than 5.2 metres long and 2 metres wide

It has no rear window, will not fit into a UK parking space and – starting at £130,000 – ($172,000) is aimed squarely at rich tech industry buyers driving the wide open roads of America.

Jaguar’s electric car, the Type 01, was launched in New York on Tuesday night and marks the culmination of a two-year rebrand that has been one of the most scrutinised in automotive history.

Continue reading...
title: Jaguar targets young Americans with Type 01 EV – but it’s too long for UK parking spaces
